Rishi / Kim —

Following our demo last week, Vectoris (Jamie) shared their MSA + order form for the POC and potential pilot. Attaching the docs they sent. High level: they want to start with a 3-month pilot, run in us-west, and will ingest small volumes of PII-ish telemetry for feature testing (we flagged processing restrictions).

Can legal help with an initial pass on:
- Which template to use (Redwood MSA v2 vs v3) — v3 has simplified indemnity language but we need to confirm compatibility with their procurement team.
- Any non-starter redlines (audit frequency, data residency, indemnity cap, IP ownership of model outputs).
- Order form fields we should lock before sending back (billing contact, PO language, payment terms — they mentioned 60 days).

Attachments: Vectoris_MSA_Draft_v1.docx (their redline), Vectoris_Order_Form_0426.xlsx (blank order form)

Timeline: Jamie is hoping for a returned redline by end of next week (4/25). If that’s tight, please call out must-have vs nice-to-have changes so Marissa can negotiate scope.

Marissa — thanks for the context. Looping legal (Kim) is correct. A few immediate items from sales/procurement side:
- Confirmed bill-to: Vectoris Labs, Attn: Accounts Payable — Laura Chen (laura.chen@vectoris.com) — I asked Jamie to confirm.
- Payment term preference: 60 days (Jamie mentioned this on the call). If we can’t accept 60d, Marissa to escalate to me before countering at 30d.
- Pilot scope: limited ingestion; include explicit data handling exhibit and audit cadence (quarterly limited-scope SOC evidence + on-site audit only if triggered).

I’ve attached a quick party-sheet (party-sheet.csv) and our recommended baseline: redwood_msa_v3.docx. Kim — please prioritize a first-pass redline focused on: data residency, audit rights, indemnity cap (we usually target 5x fees up to $1M for pilots), and a short IP carveout for model outputs (customer-generated prompts/labels vs Redwood model improvements).

Suggested timeline: initial legal redline by 4/21 so Marissa can start commercial negotiations; final back-and-forth by 4/25. If you need a call, happy to join.

Subject: Re: Intake: Vectoris MSA & Order Form — party details + template choice

Thanks Rishi / Marissa — I reviewed the Vectoris draft quickly and flagged the following as near-term concerns that we should either push back on or propose alternate language for: 

1) Indemnity / Cap: Vectoris uses uncapped indemnity for third-party claims arising from data. For a pilot with PII-ish telemetry we should propose a cap: 5x fees up to $1M, and narrow to claims arising from Redwood’s breach of contract/third-party IP.

2) Audit rights / SOC evidence: their draft requests annual on-site audits at vendor expense. We can offer quarterly SOC 2 Type II evidence upload + remote evidence review; limit on-site requests to material incidents. Also need to clarify scope (systems vs customer-defined dataset).

3) Data residency & subprocessors: their MSA references EU residency but the pilot is in us-west. We should lock region (us-west) in Exhibit A and require notice + approval for any cross-border processing. Add subprocessor list and 30-day notice for changes.

4) IP / Model outputs: they try to claim ownership of model outputs. Propose retention: customer owns labels and prompts they provide; Redwood retains model weight/tech improvements. Add narrow license to customer for internal use of outputs.

5) Payment terms / PO language: Vectoris wants a single aggregated invoice at pilot end. Confirm whether we will accept milestone billing for pilot or prefer monthly.

I’ll prepare a tracked redline against redwood_msa_v3.docx and highlight must-haves vs negotiables. If Rishi/Marissa can confirm billing contact and whether they’ll accept our 30-day default, I’ll prioritize the redline for 4/21 delivery.

Regards,

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts

Thanks all — quick answers from our side: 
- Billing contact: Laura Chen <laura.chen@vectoris.com> (Accounts Payable).
- Payment terms: procurement prefers Net 60 but can escalate if required — please flag if Redwood needs Net 30.
- Audit / SOC: Vectoris can provide SOC 2 Type II reports and is comfortable with remote evidence review; on-site audits would be escalated and are rare.
- IP: Vectoris is mainly concerned about being able to use model outputs internally; ownership beyond that is negotiable.

Attached a signed PO stub to indicate commercial intent (signed_po_stub.pdf). We’re happy to review Redwood’s redline and iterate. Let me know if you want a short call Monday to walk the changes.
